data.detail:

This release required three separate CI-red holds before pinning, each a genuinely different root cause, none reproducible on Vince's local machine:
1. bf8aa64 (2026-09-09): pyright baseline-ratchet failure (3 errors vs baseline 0) — fixed by an open()-instead-of-Path.read_text(newline="") portability fix (that keyword is 3.13-only, project requires >=3.11) plus pyright extraPaths=["tools"] for tests importing renderers after a runtime sys.path.insert.
2. aeca997 -> fixed in 967cfd7: chromadb concurrent-open race, AttributeError "'RustBindingsAPI' object has no attribute 'bindings'" during concurrent PersistentClient opens on Windows, wrapped by chromadb into ValueError "Could not connect to tenant default_tenant" — matched an already-open task (7ec1e5929309, filed 2026-07-15) that had named this exact fix. Fixed by widening _retry_chromadb_open's retry predicate to match on message (not exception type) for both error shapes, while still letting genuine NotFoundError/misconfigured-tenant errors propagate on first attempt. Task 7ec1e5929309 left open — this mitigates the race, does not root-cause it.
3. 967cfd7 -> fixed in 9896d71: tests/test_wp_sidecar.py::test_sidecar_dies_within_bound_when_its_server_dies timed out on a `powershell Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` WMI query that itself could stall on hosted Windows runners. Fixed by replacing the subprocess+WMI child-process lookup with an in-process ctypes CreateToolhelp32Snapshot call — deliberately not just raising the timeout, since a stalling observation tool inside a latency-bound assertion corrupts the measurement itself.

What's in 0.37.0 (user-facing): graph identity resolution/enforcement — writes refused when no email resolves from any source, new cognition_set_identity tool to confirm who is driving a checkout, SVN credentials read file-only as suggestions that never attribute a write, and a vibe-cognition-remap-identity CLI to correct already-recorded attribution. Also carries the 0.36.3 fix where the hygiene pass writes .cognition/.gitignore in non-git (e.g. SVN) working copies.

Each of the three holds was verified independently before reporting back to Vince (never trusting the relayed short SHA or his local green run), and each fix was confirmed against fresh CI before pinning. data.summary: SVN setup guide for vibe-cognition (shipped in v0.38.0 through v0.38.2) instructed users to strip the trailing slash from chromadb/ in .cognition/.gitignore while leaving it on local/ (which holds identity.json), but SVN ignore globs are fnmatch patterns with no directory-only meaning, so local/ with a trailing slash matches nothing and a bare local is required.
data.detail:
Since v0.38.0 moved the team roster and identity data into per-person profile files, .cognition/.gitignore carries two entries meant to stay untracked in SVN: chromadb/ and local/ (local/ holds identity.json, containing a person's name and email). The SVN setup guide told readers "ONE EDIT IS REQUIRED WHILE COPYING: strip the trailing slash from chromadb/" -- correctly calling out chromadb/ but never mentioning that the same fix is needed for local/. Because SVN's svn:ignore uses fnmatch-style globs with no directory-only semantics (unlike gitignore's trailing-slash convention), a pattern of local/ with the trailing slash intact matches nothing at all -- verified in Vince's validation lab. Any SVN team following the guide literally therefore left local/ effectively unignored, so their next `svn add --force` committed a teammate's name and email into version control: precisely the PII leak the local/ relocation in v0.38.0 was designed to prevent, caused by the setup guide's own incomplete instruction rather than by any code defect.

Fixed in v0.38.3 (commit 241d4ceafd3b525bca44887856c1e92e2a4d7b33, pinned in colton-claude-plugins at 136b845cf25a1e067f4280cbbeae60e1d1e8492a). The known affected parties are Burke and Jon-Paul's SVN team, who set up vibe-cognition following the v0.38.0-v0.38.2 guide; they may already have identity.json under version control and need to be warned to check their repository history and purge it if present. Colton was notified directly (outside the graph) to reach out to them, since this needs human follow-up on repositories vibe-cognition's own tooling cannot see or fix.

The MCP server now pins PYTHONPATH to the installed code so a plugin update can no longer leave a stale server version running unnoticed. cognition_load_project is now actually read-only (previously it was not, despite being documented as such).
